name: armagetronad-web
description: Node-side runtime dependencies for the Armagetron Advanced WebAssembly port. Not a JS project: nothing here is built or published, and the wasm artifact is produced by web/Makefile.
comment: ws is required by Emscripten itself, not by any code in this repo. Its socket emulation implements BSD sockets over WebSockets and reaches for the npm package by name in two places (deps/emsdk/upstream/emscripten/src/lib/libsockfs.js:278 for outgoing peers, :581 for the listening server). Without it the first bind() raises a Node MODULE_NOT_FOUND out of the JS glue, which unwinds straight through the wasm frames and kills the process before any C++ handler can see it. This file lives in web/ rather than the repo root so the port keeps its footprint inside web/; Node's resolver walks up from web/dist-m0/ and finds web/node_modules on the way.
deployComment: `npm run deploy` publishes web/dist-m1/ to the repository's gh-pages branch. It does NOT build: run `source deps/emsdk/emsdk_env.sh && make -f web/Makefile client -j8` from the repo root first, or you will publish whatever stale artefacts dist-m1 happens to hold. npm runs scripts with this file's directory as the working directory, which is why the paths are web/-relative. index.html is the site-root redirect (see the comment inside it): emcc names the page armagetronad.html, and GitHub Pages serves a directory URL from index.html only, so without the copy the Pages root answers with GitHub's 404. The two flags are not decoration. `-f` is gh-pages' --no-history: without it every deploy appends a commit that still carries the previous 5 MB of binaries, so the branch grows by the whole artefact set each time; with it the branch is force-pushed as a single parentless commit and the repository stays one deploy's worth of blobs (the old ones become unreachable). `--nojekyll` writes the .nojekyll file that turns off Pages' Jekyll build -- Jekyll is what would otherwise refuse to serve underscore-prefixed paths and could rewrite files it thinks are templates. Nothing in this artefact set is underscore-prefixed today, so the flag is insurance, not a fix for an observed failure. gh-pages is invoked through npx rather than added to dependencies on purpose: this package exists only so Node can resolve `ws` for Emscripten's socket layer (see the comment above), and a deploy tool is not a runtime dependency of anything. The major version is pinned so a future gh-pages 7 cannot change the meaning of these flags under a deploy nobody re-read.

scripts.deploy: cp index.html dist-m1/index.html && npx --yes gh-pages@6 -d dist-m1 -f --nojekyll -m "Deploy $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
